attachments.text:
EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT (extract)

between
Birkenrain Trading Ltd, St. Gallen, represented by Anna Moser, Sales Director (employer)
and
Peter Baumann, Schulhausstrasse 58, 9000 St. Gallen (employee)

1. Start of employment
The employment begins on 23 March 2026 and is concluded for an unlimited period.

2. Position
Sales representative, region Eastern Switzerland, full-time.

3. Salary
CHF 3,350 gross per month plus commission according to annex.

4. Probation period
The first two months of employment are a probation period.

5. Notice period
After the probation period, the employment may be terminated by either party with three months' notice to the end of a calendar month.

St. Gallen, 10 March 2026

For the employer: Anna Moser
Employee: Peter Baumann

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Was the notice given while the probation period was still running, counting any extension of the probation period under art. 335b para. 3 (a probation period interrupted by illness, accident or a non-voluntary legal obligation is extended accordingly)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Was the employee performing Swiss compulsory military service, civil defence service or alternative civilian service on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running, or, for such a service lasting more than eleven days, did either of those fall within the four weeks before or after it?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual agreement, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract set a probation period other than the first month of employment?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Was the employee, through no fault of their own, wholly or partly prevented from working by illness or accident on the day notice was given or at some time while the notice period was running, and was the incapacity at that point still within its protected length: up to 30 days in the first year of service, 90 days in the second to fifth years, 180 days from the sixth year?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Where a protected period (illness or accident, compulsory service, pregnancy or birth, as above) is raised: was the notice given before that period began, with the notice period not yet expired when it began?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Was the employee pregnant, or within sixteen weeks after giving birth, on the day notice was given or while the notice period was running?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Does the file say that a written individual employment contract, a standard employment contract or a collective employment contract sets notice periods different from the statutory ones (seven days during probation, art. 335b para. 1; one month in the first year of service, two months in the second to ninth years, three months thereafter)?

text:
Hi,

Birkenrain Trading Ltd has given me notice. On 9 June 2026 Anna Moser, the sales director, called me into a meeting room in St. Gallen and handed me a letter saying my employment was being terminated. She said the sales figures in my region were 'not where they should be'. My colleague Ian Weber was let go the same week.

I started there on 23 March 2026, and my trial period ended on 22 May, so by the time she handed me that letter I was no longer on trial. That much is clear.

I've attached my contract.

The contract sets its own trial period of two months instead of the usual one month. I didn't think much about it when I signed.

What matters more to me is the notice. The contract says that once the trial period is over, either side has to give three months' notice to the end of a month. I specifically asked for that when I signed, because I was leaving a safe job. It's far longer than the one month you'd normally get in the first year.

I earn CHF 3,350 a month. When does my job actually end, and what do I do if they try to pay me for less?

Thanks,
Peter Baumann
Schulhausstrasse 58, St. Gallen
